Save the session -- the structure, the bonds you drew, the view, the selection and the measurements -- over the file this is, without asking where
Save the session under another name
Write a file for something else to read -- a CIF, an XYZ.  One way: it never becomes this document's file
One unit cell with its bonds, as a mesh a 3D printer can take.  Blender does the meshing, so it has to be installed -- see Preferences > Engines
The net drawn on this structure as a .cgd file, for Systre to name -- a second opinion on the Net panel that does not come from the code that gave the first
Write this molecule into the folder the MOF builder reads, so it appears in the block picker beside the 867 PORMAKE ships.  It needs connection points on it -- the dialog says what is missing.
A folder that structures and their calculations live in
Every open structure.  Each modified one still asks
Everything this application remembers between sessions -- where new workspaces go, and what a newly opened structure is drawn as
Delete whichever is selected: the bonds if bonds are, otherwise the sites
Suppress the selected bonds, and their whole symmetry orbit
Escape, when there is no gesture or mode to leave first
Select every bond joining two elements, and no atoms -- so Delete and Bond type act on those bonds alone
Put an atom at the middle of the selected atoms -- a dummy atom, which bonds to nothing and is what net edges and measurements are drawn to, or an element
Replace the selected atoms with one at their middle -- of their element when they share one, a dummy atom when they do not.  Whole orbits go, as with Delete, and the new atom is bonded to nothing
Complete every main-group coordination with the hydrogens an X-ray structure never had

Build a molecule from a SMILES string and paste it into this structure.  It arrives with the bonds the builder gave it and no others, and pasting into a group with symmetry multiplies it -- the dialog says by how much before you press the button.

Put copies of a molecule -- from another tab or a file -- into the empty space of this structure, each where it touches nothing.  A host with symmetry is reduced to P1 first, and bonds are not recalculated

Thread copies of this framework through its own pores: every placement the lattice allows is measured, and one where atoms of two copies would meet cannot be chosen.  The copies keep their bonds, and the result is in P1

Make a deposited structure one a calculation can use: order the disorder into whole atoms, remove solvent, complete M3O trimers, add the missing hydrogens and take the primitive cell -- each step saying what it chose before anything is done, and one undo step for the lot

Turn each selected atom that has exactly one bond into a connection point: a dummy 0.75 A along that bond, which is what a PORMAKE building block is joined by.  There is no unmark -- an X does not remember what it was, so the way back is Ctrl+Z.

Collapse the selected atoms into a single connection point, 0.75 A from the middle of everything they were bonded to and carrying those bonds.  For a chelate: two atoms that meet the next block together are one joint, and marking them separately gives a block with twice the coordination number it has.
Which atoms bond, and how close they have to be
Perceive the bonds again from the geometry as it is now.  Bonds do not change on their own when atoms move; this is what changes them.

Drop the bonds you drew and the ones you deleted, and take what the distance criteria give.  The only way back from a deleted bond once the undo stack has gone, because a deletion is saved with the project.
Re-perceive the bonds after every edit that moves an atom, instead of only when you ask
Call the selected bonds single, and their whole symmetry orbit with them
Call the selected bonds double, and their whole symmetry orbit with them
Call the selected bonds triple, and their whole symmetry orbit with them
Call the selected bonds aromatic, and their whole symmetry orbit with them
Let the geometry decide this bond's order again
click an atom or bond · shift-click to add · double-click for the whole fragment
drag a box over the atoms - shift to add - everything inside is taken, bonds included, front to back
click to place an atom · click an atom to build from it, then keep clicking to chain · Escape stops
click two atoms to bond them · click a bond to remove it
click two atoms to draw a net edge - click an edge to select it, Del removes it
drag an atom to move it, or any atom of the selection to move all of it - alt-drag turns the selection - shift-alt-drag moves it in depth - the background still turns the crystal
click a bond for its length, or 2 atoms for a distance, 3 for an angle, 4 for a torsion
Detect the space group at a tolerance and adopt it
Choose a group and generate or impose it
Drop to a maximal subgroup so that an orbit splits and its atoms become independent
Rebuild in the conventional setting of the detected group
Merge sites of the same element that are the same atom, symmetry images included
The same crystal in the other hand: the coordinates and the space group together
Expand every symmetry orbit into independent sites
Change the cell parameters, keeping fractional or cartesian coordinates
na x nb x nc, or a general integer transformation
The shortest, most orthogonal basis for this cell
Measure the selected atoms in the order they were picked: two a distance, three an angle about the middle one, four a torsion -- or the length of every selected bond
Fit a plane through the selected atoms: exactly through three, least-squares through more
Measure the angle between the planes defined so far -- one measurement per pair
Atoms at half their covalent radius, tubes for bonds
Ball and stick, with every shared or partly empty site cut into wedges -- one per occupant, and a grey one for the vacancy
Bond-width tubes with matching spheres at the joints
Bonds as lines, no atom geometry

Atoms at their van der Waals radius
Atoms as displacement ellipsoids at the probability level set in the style panel -- the picture that makes a bad refinement obvious
Coordination polyhedra for the nodes and tubes for everything else -- an MOF's metals and its linkers in the same picture
Coordination polyhedra as translucent hulls, coloured by the atom at the centre
The ellipsoid plot a structure report is checked in: pale outlined atoms, thin dark bonds and no highlight -- what PLATON and checkCIF draw
Flat colour inside a dark outline, and no shading at all -- the one style that exports as plain circles and strokes an illustrator can recolour
Draw a double bond as two tubes and a triple as three, with an inner dashed line for an aromatic one
Draw the net a chemist marked out over the framework -- thicker and translucent, over the real bonds rather than in place of them
The triad in the corner of the view: which way a, b and c point as the structure turns

Draw what a porosity run found: the largest pore where it sits, and the channels it belongs to.  Nothing is drawn until Modules > Zeo++ has answered
A ruler in the corner, in Angstrom.  It measures the camera and not the crystal, so a cell that contracts during a relaxation is seen to contract against it
Take a DFTB+ run's atom colouring and orbital lobes off the picture.  They go by themselves when the atoms move

params.label: Atom radii
params.accepts: one of Zeo++'s own table (what its papers used), Van der Waals radii (this application's table), Covalent radii (this application's table)
params.help: Every number Zeo++ returns is a function of how big it thinks the atoms are.  Whichever is chosen is written into the log.

params.name: radii_file
params.label: Radii file
params.help: Your own two-column table (element, radius in A), which overrides the choice above when it is set

actions.name: volume
actions.label: Accessible volume...
actions.tip: How much of the cell a gas molecule can occupy, which is the pore volume a paper quotes

params.name: gas
params.label: Probe
params.accepts: one of Nitrogen, N2 (1.86 A), Argon, Ar (1.72 A), Carbon dioxide, CO2 (1.65 A), Hydrogen, H2 (1.48 A), Helium, He (1.30 A), Methane, CH4 (1.86 A), Use the radius below
params.help: Nitrogen is what a pore volume is usually quoted to.  A radius quoted without the probe it was measured with means nothing.

params.name: probe_radius
params.label: Probe radius
params.help: Used only when the probe above is set to 'Use the radius below'

params.name: channel_radius
params.label: Channel radius
params.help: Which channels count as reachable.  Zero means 'the same as the probe', which is what makes the answer the one the probe would measure.

params.name: occupiable
params.label: Probe-occupiable volume
params.help: Zeo++'s -volpo: the volume the probe occupies rather than the volume its centre can reach.  The larger of the two, and the one a paper means by pore volume.

params.name: samples
params.label: Samples
params.help: Monte Carlo points across the whole cell.  50000 is what the published figures use.

params.name: draw
params.label: Draw the accessible surface
params.help: Put the boundary of that volume into the 3D view: the surface a probe of this radius can push its centre up to.  Computed here and not by Zeo++, at the same probe and the same radii.

params.name: spacing
params.label: Surface detail
params.help: Grid spacing for the surface.  Smaller is finer and slower: 0.5 A is a second and 190 000 triangles on MFU-4l, 0.3 A is eight times that.

params.name: radii
params.label: Atom radii
params.accepts: one of Zeo++'s own table (what its papers used), Van der Waals radii (this application's table), Covalent radii (this application's table)
params.help: Every number Zeo++ returns is a function of how big it thinks the atoms are.  Whichever is chosen is written into the log.

params.name: radii_file
params.label: Radii file
params.help: Your own two-column table (element, radius in A), which overrides the choice above when it is set

params.name: high_accuracy
params.label: High accuracy
params.help: Zeo++'s -ha: add Voronoi vertices so that atoms of different radii are treated properly.  Slower, and what the documentation recommends.

actions.name: volume-grid
actions.label: Accessible volume (faster)...
actions.tip: The same volume in a second or two -- MFU-4l's occupiable volume is 1.7 s here against 71 s in Zeo++ -- read off this application's own grid.  A window within a grid step of the probe's size is flagged rather than guessed.

params.name: gas
params.label: Probe
params.accepts: one of Nitrogen, N2 (1.86 A), Argon, Ar (1.72 A), Carbon dioxide, CO2 (1.65 A), Hydrogen, H2 (1.48 A), Helium, He (1.30 A), Methane, CH4 (1.86 A), Use the radius below
params.help: Nitrogen is what a pore volume is usually quoted to.  A radius quoted without the probe it was measured with means nothing.

params.name: probe_radius
params.label: Probe radius
params.help: Used only when the probe above is set to 'Use the radius below'

params.name: occupiable
params.label: Probe-occupiable volume
params.help: The volume the probe occupies rather than the volume its centre can reach: the pore volume a paper quotes.  It reads up to 0.03 of the cell above Zeo++'s -volpo, which falls short of the union of probe spheres.

params.name: draw
params.label: Draw the accessible surface
params.help: Put the channels' surface into the 3D view: the same grid the numbers come from.

params.name: spacing
params.label: Grid spacing
params.help: Finer is slower and resolves narrower windows: 0.4 A is a second or two on MFU-4l.  A window within half a step of the probe's size is flagged in the table rather than guessed.

params.name: radii
params.label: Atom radii
params.accepts: one of Zeo++'s own table (what its papers used), Van der Waals radii (this application's table), Covalent radii (this application's table)
params.help: Every number Zeo++ returns is a function of how big it thinks the atoms are.  Whichever is chosen is written into the log.

params.name: radii_file
params.label: Radii file
params.help: Your own two-column table (element, radius in A), which overrides the choice above when it is set

actions.name: psd
actions.label: Pore size distribution...
actions.tip: How much of the pore space sits at each diameter, as a histogram

params.name: gas
params.label: Probe
params.accepts: one of Nitrogen, N2 (1.86 A), Argon, Ar (1.72 A), Carbon dioxide, CO2 (1.65 A), Hydrogen, H2 (1.48 A), Helium, He (1.30 A), Methane, CH4 (1.86 A), Use the radius below
params.help: A small probe resolves narrow pores; a large one only sees what it fits into, which is why this one defaults to a radius rather than to a gas.  A radius quoted without the probe it was measured with means nothing.

params.name: probe_radius
params.label: Probe radius
params.help: Used only when the probe above is set to 'Use the radius below'

params.name: channel_radius
params.label: Channel radius
params.help: Which channels count as reachable.  Zero means 'the same as the probe', which is what makes the answer the one the probe would measure.

params.name: samples
params.label: Samples
params.help: Monte Carlo points across the whole cell, and the one parameter that decides how long this takes: 20000 is minutes on a framework and enough to see the shape; the published figures use 50000.

params.name: radii
params.label: Atom radii
params.accepts: one of Zeo++'s own table (what its papers used), Van der Waals radii (this application's table), Covalent radii (this application's table)
params.help: Every number Zeo++ returns is a function of how big it thinks the atoms are.  Whichever is chosen is written into the log.

params.name: radii_file
params.label: Radii file
params.help: Your own two-column table (element, radius in A), which overrides the choice above when it is set

params.name: high_accuracy
params.label: High accuracy
params.help: Zeo++'s -ha: add Voronoi vertices so that atoms of different radii are treated properly.  Slower, and what the documentation recommends.

modules.name: mof
modules.label: MOF builder
modules.description: Build a framework from a topology, a metal node and a linker, with PORMAKE.  The result opens in a new tab with its net already drawn.

actions.name: build
actions.label: Build a framework...
actions.tip: Pick a net, a node and a linker; the framework opens in a new tab

params.name: topology
params.label: Topology
params.help: The net to build on, by its RCSR name -- pcu, tbo, soc.  2399 of them ship with PORMAKE.

params.name: nodes
params.label: Node building blocks
params.help: Which block goes in which node slot: 'N59' when the net has one kind of node, or '0=N19,1=N59' when it has more.  A block fits a slot only when it has as many connection points as the slot is coordinated.

params.name: edges
params.label: Linkers
params.help: Which linker goes on which kind of edge: 'E32', or '0-0=E32,0-1=E14'.  Left empty the nodes are joined directly, which is what PORMAKE builds for a net with no linker in it.

params.name: repeat
params.label: Repeat the net
params.help: How many times to tile the net before anything is placed on it -- '2x2x2', or '2' for the same in all three.  A framework built on a repeated net is the same material in a larger cell, which is what a defect, a guest or an interpenetrated pair needs room for.  Leave it at 1x1x1 for the net itself.

params.name: orientation
params.label: Node orientation
params.accepts: one of Consistent across every joint, As found by the fit
params.help: Which way round the node blocks go.  A symmetric node fits its slot equally well two dozen ways.  By default each node is turned so that the faces at the two ends of every linker agree -- carboxylate against carboxylate, chelate against chelate -- which is what makes MOF-5's clusters alternate on a 2x2x2 net, and only where that is measurably better than what the fit chose.  'As found' keeps whatever the fit reached first, exactly as PORMAKE builds it.

params.name: spacing
params.label: Interlayer spacing
params.help: How far apart the sheets of a layer net are stacked, in Angstrom.  Left empty it is 3.4, which is where pi-stacked sheets sit -- Ni3(HITP)2 is 3.24.  Only a layer net such as hcb, hxl, sql or kgm has sheets to stack, and a spacing given for any other net is refused.

params.name: offset
params.label: Stacking offset
params.help: Where each sheet sits over the one below, as two fractions of the net's own a and b -- '1/3, 2/3', or '0.5, 0'.  Left empty the sheets are eclipsed, one directly over the next.  Layer nets only, like the spacing.

params.name: interpenetration
params.label: Interpenetration
params.help: How many copies of the framework, threaded through one another -- 2 for two-fold.  The copies go where the most room is, measured by the closest contact between them, and a framework too dense for any placement is refused rather than built crowded.  Structure > Interpenetrate lists every placement.

params.name: topology_dir
params.label: Extra topologies
params.help: A folder of your own .cgd nets, read alongside the ones PORMAKE ships

params.name: bb_dir
params.label: Extra building blocks
params.help: A folder of your own .xyz building blocks, whose connection points are listed on the second line

modules.name: build
modules.label: Molecule builder
modules.description: Build a molecule from a SMILES string, with RDKit.  It opens in a tab of its own, in a box with enough vacuum around it to relax in.

actions.name: molecule
actions.label: Molecule from SMILES...
actions.tip: Build a molecule; it opens in a new tab

params.name: smiles
params.label: SMILES
params.help: The molecule, as SMILES -- c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-] is benzoate.  A '*' marks a connection point, and [*:1] and [*:2] say which is which.

params.name: name
params.label: Name
params.help: What to call it, in the tab and in the block file.  The SMILES string itself when this is left empty.

params.name: optimise
params.label: Relax it
params.help: Relax the embedded geometry with MMFF, or UFF where MMFF has no parameters for it.  The force field in this application takes it further.

params.name: seed
params.label: Conformer seed
params.help: Which conformer comes out.  Fixed rather than random so that the same string twice is the same molecule; change it to be offered another one.

modules.name: pxrd
modules.label: PXRD
modules.description: Calculate a powder X-ray diffraction pattern from the structure: peak positions from the cell and the space group, intensities from the atoms through structure factors.  The pattern is written as .xy beside the indexed reflection list, and a measured pattern can be overlaid on it.

actions.name: simulate
actions.label: Simulate a pattern...
actions.tip: Calculate a powder diffraction pattern from this structure

params.name: source
params.label: Radiation
params.accepts: one of Cu Ka1 (1.5406 A), Cu Ka average (1.5418 A), Mo Ka1 (0.7093 A), Co Ka1 (1.7890 A), Ag Ka1 (0.5594 A), Use the wavelength below
params.help: Which tube the pattern is calculated for.  2-theta moves when this does, so a pattern compared with a measurement has to be calculated for the same source.

params.name: wavelength
params.label: Wavelength
params.help: Used only when the radiation above is 'Use the wavelength below'.

params.name: two_theta_min
params.label: 2-theta from
params.help: Below about half a degree the Lorentz-polarisation factor diverges and no instrument measures, so that is the floor.

params.name: two_theta_max
params.label: 2-theta to
params.help: A wider range is more reflections and a longer calculation.  Fifty degrees is where a laboratory MOF pattern stops being worth plotting.

params.name: step
params.label: Step
params.help: The 2-theta grid the profiles are summed onto.  It has to be several times finer than the peak width or the peaks come out as spikes.

params.name: shape
params.label: Peak shape
params.help: Pseudo-Voigt is the usual choice for laboratory data: a Lorentzian fraction mixed with a Gaussian, approximating the convolution of sample and instrument broadening.

params.name: eta
params.label: Lorentzian fraction
params.help: The Pseudo-Voigt mixing parameter: 0 is a pure Gaussian and 1 a pure Lorentzian.  Ignored by the other two shapes.

params.name: caglioti_u
params.label: Caglioti U
params.help: Peak width against angle: FWHM^2 = U tan^2(theta) + V tan(theta) + W, in degrees squared.  The three defaults are a typical laboratory diffractometer.

params.name: caglioti_v
params.label: Caglioti V
params.help: The linear term of the width relation.  Often negative, which is why a very low-angle peak can come out with no width at all and is dropped.

params.name: caglioti_w
params.label: Caglioti W
params.help: The constant term, which is most of the width at low angle.

params.name: b_overall
params.label: Overall B
params.help: One thermal displacement parameter for every atom: exp(-2 B sin^2(theta) / lambda^2).  Left at zero the high-angle peaks come out systematically too strong against a published pattern; 1 to 3 A^2 is typical.

params.name: show_absences
params.label: Mark systematic absences
params.help: Draw a second comb under the pattern, in its own colour, where this space group forbids a reflection.  An unexpected peak is either an impurity or the wrong space group, and which one depends on whether it sits over a forbidden position.  A structure in P1 has none, because P1 forbids nothing.

modules.name: scan
modules.label: Energy scan
modules.description: Walk one or two coordinates and relax everything else at each point, to map the energy landscape of a flexible structure.  An axis is a lattice parameter, the cell volume, or an internal coordinate -- a distance, an angle, a dihedral, or the angle between two planes -- and it is held by a constraint rather than by freezing the atoms that define it.  Every point is left behind as a structure to open.

actions.name: run
actions.label: Relaxed scan...
actions.tip: Map the energy landscape over one or two coordinates

params.name: engine
params.label: Engine
params.help: Which energy engine relaxes each point.  For a flexible framework a machine-learned potential is the better choice: UFF4MOF was never fitted to reproduce a breathing double well.

params.name: axis1
params.label: First axis
params.help: A cell parameter (a, b, c, alpha, beta, gamma), 'volume', or an internal coordinate over P1 atom indices: 'distance 0, 5', 'angle 0, 1, 2', 'torsion 0, 1, 2, 3', 'plane 0+1+2, 6+7+8'.  Atoms joined by '+' are their centroid, and it follows them.

params.name: axis2
params.label: Second axis
params.help: Leave empty for a one-dimensional scan.  A cell parameter (a, b, c, alpha, beta, gamma), 'volume', or an internal coordinate over P1 atom indices: 'distance 0, 5', 'angle 0, 1, 2', 'torsion 0, 1, 2, 3', 'plane 0+1+2, 6+7+8'.  Atoms joined by '+' are their centroid, and it follows them.

params.name: seed
params.label: Starting geometry
params.accepts: one of Carry on from the nearest point, Restart from this structure
params.help: Carrying the last relaxed geometry into the next cell is what makes a scan affordable, and it is also what makes it path-dependent: near a transition the optimiser stays in the basin it arrived in.

params.name: direction
params.label: Direction
params.accepts: one of Both, and report each, Forwards only, Backwards only
params.help: Walking the grid both ways and drawing both is how hysteresis shows up instead of hiding in one curve.

params.name: method
params.label: Optimiser
params.accepts: one of abnr, conjugate_gradient, fire, lbfgs, quasi_newton, smart, steepest_descent
params.help: Smart descends steeply at first and changes rule as the forces fall, which is what a scan wants: every point after the first starts near a minimum, but the first one may not.

params.name: max_steps
params.label: Steps per point
params.help: A point that stops at the limit is reported as not converged and drawn apart, so this is a ceiling rather than a target.

params.name: pre_engine
params.label: Pre-relax with
params.help: A cheaper engine run at every point before the one the landscape is of -- UFF4MOF ahead of MACE, say.  A volume step moves every atom with the cell, and this spends the long walk back at the cheap price.  Only the main engine's energy is reported.

params.name: pre_tolerance
params.label: Pre-relaxation tolerance
params.help: Loose on purpose: the cheap engine's minimum is not the one wanted, so converging to it tightly buys nothing.

modules.name: net
modules.label: Net builder
modules.description: Draw a named RCSR net -- a vertex is a hydrogen and an edge is a string of heliums, which is notation and not chemistry.  It opens in a tab of its own, with coordination polyhedra ready to draw over the vertices.

actions.name: draw
actions.label: Draw a net...
actions.tip: Draw a named RCSR net; it opens in a new tab

params.name: net
params.label: Net
params.help: The RCSR's own name for it -- pcu, dia, srs, acs, sod, rht, hcb.  2926 of them can be drawn, the 200 layers among them; the four with no cell cannot.

params.name: scale
params.label: Cell scale
params.help: The .cgd cells are normalised so an edge is about one unit long.  Eight puts the atoms along an edge about 1 A apart, which is what makes the edges read as rods.

params.name: beads
params.label: Atoms per edge
params.help: Counting the two nodes.  More is a smoother rod and a bigger structure; the atom next to a node is what a coordination polyhedron is drawn over, so there has to be at least one between them.

modules.name: blender
modules.label: Blender
modules.description: Blender, run headless, for what it can make of a structure.

actions.name: export-stl
actions.label: Export as STL...
actions.tip: One unit cell with its bonds, turned into a printable mesh by Blender

params.name: output
params.label: Save as
params.help: Where the STL goes.  A copy also stays in the run folder, beside the PDB it was made from

params.name: bonded_partners
params.label: Complete bonds across the cell faces
params.help: Bring in the atom at the far end of every bond that leaves the cell, so a linker cut by a face prints with both its ends

params.name: ball_scale
params.label: Ball scale
params.help: Atomic radii times this

params.name: h_scale
params.label: Hydrogen scale
params.help: Hydrogens again times this: at atomic radii they are too small to print

params.name: remesh
params.label: Remesh into one solid
params.help: Weld the balls and sticks into one watertight mesh.  Off leaves overlapping pieces, which most slicers refuse

params.name: voxel_size
params.label: Voxel size
params.help: The remesh grid.  Smaller keeps more detail and costs memory as the cube of it

params.name: max_tris
params.label: Triangle budget
params.help: The remesh is coarsened until the mesh fits.  0 is no budget; a binary STL is about 50 bytes a triangle

params.name: target_size
params.label: Longest side
params.help: Scale the model so its longest side is this.  0 leaves one Angstrom as one millimetre

engines.name: uff
engines.label: UFF
engines.description: Universal Force Field (Rappe et al. 1992) -- covers the whole periodic table, native and in-process

options.name: parameter_set
options.label: Parameters
options.accepts: one of UFF4MOF (UFF plus framework nodes), UFF (Rappe 1992 only)
options.help: UFF4MOF adds rows fitted to metal nodes in frameworks and types everything else exactly as UFF does.  Plain UFF never uses them, which is how to see what they change.

options.name: coulomb
options.label: Include electrostatics
options.help: Off by default, as in UFF itself: the published parameters were fitted without a Coulomb term.

options.name: charges
options.label: Charges from
options.accepts: one of The sites, Equilibrate (QEq), Equilibrate (EQeq), All zero
options.help: Only used when electrostatics are on.

options.name: vdw_cutoff
options.label: van der Waals cutoff
options.help: The pair count goes as the cube of this: 10 A is 42% fewer pairs than 12 A, for an LJ tail worth about a thousandth of a kcal/mol per pair.

options.name: skin
options.label: Neighbour list skin
options.help: How far an atom may move before the pair list is rebuilt.

engines.name: xtb
engines.label: xTB (GFN)
engines.description: Semiempirical tight binding and the GFN force field, through the tblite or xtb binary -- no parameter set to download and no atom typing to get right.

options.name: method
options.label: Method
options.help: GFN2-xTB is the default and the most accurate of the three; GFN1-xTB is older and more robust for metals; GFN-FF is a force field and is orders of magnitude faster, which for a framework of a few thousand atoms is the difference between a relaxation and an afternoon.  The method decides which binary runs: tblite for the two tight-binding ones and xtb for GFN-FF.

options.name: accuracy
options.label: Accuracy
options.help: The SCF convergence criterion, as a multiplier: smaller is tighter and slower.  Ignored by GFN-FF, which has no SCF.

options.name: temperature
options.label: Electronic temperature
options.help: Fermi filling.  Not zero by default, for the same reason DFTB+'s is not: a metallic framework at exactly zero has no gap to fill and the cycle oscillates rather than failing.

engines.name: mace
engines.label: MACE (machine-learned)
engines.description: A machine-learned potential in the atomic cluster expansion family.  The MACE-MP foundation models answer for a framework with no parameters to assign and no atom typing to get right, at a cost between a force field's and tight binding's.

options.name: model
options.label: Model
options.accepts: one of MACE-MPA-0 -- MPtrj + sAlex, PBE+U (recommended), MACE-MP-0b3 -- MPtrj, PBE+U, steadier under pressure, MACE-OMAT-0 -- OMat, PBE+U [ASL licence], MACE-MATPES-r2SCAN-0 -- r2SCAN, no +U [ASL licence], MACE-MH-1 -- crystals, molecules and surfaces [ASL licence], MACE-MP-MOF0 -- 127 MOFs, PBE-D3(BJ), for phonons; 26 elements [CC BY 4.0, cite], MACE-MP-0a medium -- the default before mace 0.3.10, MACE-MP-0a small -- fastest, MACE-MP-0a large, A model file of my own
options.help: The MACE-MP foundation models are fitted over the Materials Project and need nothing assigning -- they answer for a framework whose metal node UFF has no parameters for.  Each is downloaded once, to MACE's own cache.  Choose 'a model file of my own' for one you have fitted.

options.name: model_path
options.label: Model file
options.help: A .model file, for the 'my own' choice above.  Ignored by the MACE-MP models.

options.name: device
options.label: Run on
options.accepts: one of Whatever is fastest here, CPU, Apple GPU (mps), NVIDIA GPU (cuda)
options.help: A GPU is worth an order of magnitude on a framework of a few thousand atoms.  'Whatever is fastest here' asks torch what this machine has.

options.name: double_precision
options.label: Double precision
options.help: Leave this on for geometry optimisation: in single precision the model's own noise is larger than the energy differences an optimiser is reading, and the line search wanders instead of converging.

engines.name: orb
engines.label: ORB-v3 (machine-learned)
engines.description: Orbital Materials' universal potential.  Like MACE it needs no parameters assigning.  Run here without a dispersion correction, so a relaxed framework's volume differs by a percent or more from the benchmark that ranks it among the most accurate, which added D3.

options.name: model
options.label: Model
options.accepts: one of ORB-v3 -- OMat24, all neighbours within 6 A (recommended), ORB-v3 -- OMat24, 20 neighbours, faster, ORB-v3 -- MPtrj + Alexandria, all neighbours within 6 A, ORB-v3 -- MPtrj + Alexandria, 20 neighbours, faster
options.help: Conservative ORB-v3 models only: their forces are the gradient of their energy, which is what a relaxation needs.  Each is downloaded once, to orb-models' own cache.

options.name: device
options.label: Run on
options.accepts: one of The NVIDIA GPU if there is one, otherwise the CPU, CPU, NVIDIA GPU (cuda)
options.help: orb-models cannot run on an Apple GPU, so on a Mac this is the CPU.

options.name: double_precision
options.label: Double precision
options.help: Leave this on for geometry optimisation: in single precision the model's own noise is a third of the energy differences an optimiser reads.  Off is about 2.7 times faster.

engines.name: mattersim
engines.label: MatterSim (machine-learned)
engines.description: Microsoft's universal potential, an M3GNet trained across temperature and pressure.  Like MACE it needs no parameters assigning, and it is the fastest of the three.  Its authors note relatively low accuracy for organic polymeric systems, which is the linker half of a framework; run here without a dispersion correction.

options.name: model
options.label: Model
options.accepts: one of MatterSim 1M -- the smaller model, faster (recommended), MatterSim 5M -- five times the parameters, more accurate
options.help: Each is downloaded once, to ~/.local/mattersim.

options.name: device
options.label: Run on
options.accepts: one of The NVIDIA GPU if there is one, otherwise the CPU, CPU, NVIDIA GPU (cuda)
options.help: MatterSim cannot load onto an Apple GPU, so on a Mac this is the CPU.

options.name: double_precision
options.label: Double precision
options.help: Leave this on for geometry optimisation: in single precision the model's own noise is a noticeable part of the energy differences an optimiser reads.  Off is about 1.5 times faster.

engines.name: dftb
engines.label: DFTB+
engines.description: Density-functional tight binding, through the DFTB+ binary -- DFT-like and fast enough to relax a framework UFF can only approximate.

options.name: method
options.label: Hamiltonian
options.accepts: one of DFTB3 (third order, needs 3ob), SCC-DFTB (self-consistent charges), Non-SCC DFTB (fastest, no charge transfer)
options.help: The nearest thing DFTB has to a functional.  DFTB3 is third order and is what the 3ob set was fitted for; SCC-DFTB is second order and works with any set; non-SCC has no charge transfer at all and is for a first look.

options.name: parameter_directory
options.label: Parameter directory
options.help: The folder of Slater-Koster .skf files.  They are separate downloads from dftb.org -- 3ob for organics, matsci for inorganic solids.  Left empty, the DFTB_PREFIX environment variable is used.

options.name: dispersion
options.label: Dispersion
options.accepts: one of None, DFT-D3 with Becke-Johnson damping, Lennard-Jones (universal force field radii)
options.help: DFTB has no dispersion of its own, and a framework's pore size is a dispersion-bound number -- so for a porous solid this is not an optional refinement.

options.name: temperature
options.label: Electronic temperature
options.help: Fermi filling.  Not zero by default: a metallic framework at exactly zero has no gap to fill and the SCC cycle oscillates for ever rather than failing.

options.name: k_spacing
options.label: K-point spacing
options.help: The mesh is worked out from the cell: a cell twice as long gets half as many k-points along it.  Zero is the Gamma point alone, which is what a large cell wants.

options.name: angular_momentum
options.label: Angular momentum overrides
options.help: Per element, as 'Cl=d, Zn=d'.  The built-in table follows 3ob; a set that disagrees with it gives a number rather than an error, which is why this is here.
